subject.title: fix(uninstall): preserve user data when gateway removal fails

question: Should Gateway-service removal be required to reach an immediately observable unloaded state before `openclaw uninstall --all` may delete user data on every supported service-manager path?
rationale: This is an upgrade-sensitive CLI and lifecycle contract: a fail-closed data-preservation policy is desirable, but maintainers must decide whether the immediate observation is the supported cross-platform completion boundary or whether the service layer needs a bounded wait or stronger completion contract.

options.title: Require verified unloaded state
options.body: Keep the fail-closed cleanup gate and add service-contract proof that each supported implementation only resolves uninstall after the service is no longer loaded.

options.title: Use a bounded verification wait
options.body: Preserve the fail-closed policy but move platform-specific settling behavior into the service layer before reporting removal failure.

recommendation.title: Require verified unloaded state
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed cleanup gate and add service-contract proof that each supported implementation only resolves uninstall after the service is no longer loaded.
